sec: Other effects, eosinopenia clue and the cause tree · p845

items.q: The ocular effects of cortisol excess are:
items.exp: Eye: ↑ intraocular pressure — cataract and glaucoma. (Book p845)

items.q: Cortisol's anti-inflammatory action is attributed to:
items.exp: Miscellaneous: ↓ linear growth; inhibits IL-6 → anti-inflammatory action. (Book p845)

items.q: ‘Cortisol excess raises the WBC count yet the patient remains prone to infection.’
items.exp: Blood/immune: ↑ WBC count but still prone to infection; eosinopenia and ↑ thrombosis (hypercoagulable state). (Book p845)

items.q: Match the eosinophil clue — 1) Eosinopenia with +ve infection  2) Eosinopenia with −ve infection  3) Eosinophilia … A) Cushing syndrome  B) Addison's disease  C) Typhoid
items.exp: Eosinopenia with infection → typhoid; eosinopenia without infection → Cushing syndrome; eosinophilia → Addison's disease. (Book p845)

items.q: ACTH-dependent causes account for what share of Cushing's?
The single most common endogenous cause overall is:
opts: Ectopic ACTH from squamous cell carcinoma
items.exp: Pituitary ACTH-secreting adenoma (75%), a.k.a. Cushing's disease (micro/macro-adenoma), is the m/c endogenous cause overall. (Book p845)

items.q: The most common paraneoplastic (ectopic ACTH) cause is:
items.exp: Paraneoplastic tumour (15%): squamous cell carcinoma is m/c; also thymic/bronchial carcinoid, pheochromocytoma/medullary Ca thyroid. (Book p845)

items.q: The m/c cause of Cushing's in toddlers is:
items.exp: ACTH independent (10%): adrenal adenoma; adrenal carcinoma is the m/c cause in toddlers. (Book p845)

items.q: Match the McCune-Albright (GSα-subunit defect) triad — pick the correct set:
opts: Precocious puberty, fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots
Fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots, atrial myxoma
Precocious puberty, café-au-lait spots, lens dislocation
items.exp: McCune-Albright triad: precocious puberty, fibrous dysplasia, café-au-lait spots; m/c cause in infancy. (Book p845)

items.q: Primary pigmented nodular adrenal disease (PPNAD) shows ___ and is part of:
opts: Micronodular hyperplasia; Carney's complex (lentigines, atrial myxomas)
items.exp: PPNAD = micronodular hyperplasia, part of Carney's complex with lentigines and atrial myxomas. (Book p845)

items.q: In adult Cushing's the sex preponderance is:
items.exp: Adult Cushing's: F > M; diagnosis is made on the discriminatory value of symptoms. (Book p845)
